The term mandatory refers to a client requirement and means a field must be present in a message and must contain certain values. Conditional refers to a client requirement applying under specified conditions. While the V.I.P. System enforces edits and rejects transactions for some violations of mandatory requirements, V.I.P. does not enforce edits for all mandatory or conditional fields and values. Visa strongly urges clients and their processors to comply with mandatory field requirements. Failure to do so can result in greater risk to the client or increased processing cost, and may result in exposure to disputes and compliance claims, elevated decline rates, and disqualification for preferential interchange rates. Visa also advises clients not to rely on the V.I.P. System to reject all transactions not complying with mandatory or conditional requirements.

text_a: There are three types of interchange reimbursement fees (IRFs).

Domestic Interchange Reimbursement Fees—Fees paid by one participant to another for transactions acquired and issued in the same country. Intraregional Interchange Reimbursement Fees—Fees paid by one participant to another for transactions acquired and issued in different countries within the same Visa region. Interregional Interchange Reimbursement Fees—Fees paid by one participant to another for transactions acquired and issued in different Visa regions. In this context, transaction country is the country in which the transaction takes place, and issuing country is the country of the issuer of the card used in the transaction. If no domestic IRF has been established, the intraregional IRF applies. If no intraregional IRF has been established, the interregional (international) IRF applies. IRFs are settled daily through the settlement process. For National Net Settlement Service transactions, there is only one settlement currency, so balancing does not involve currency conversion. For International Settlement Service transactions, however, there are many settlement currencies. Visa uses buy and sell rates for currency conversion. These rates are paired into USD-based rates used when converting non- USD currencies against the U.S. dollar, and cross-rates (non-USD-based rates) used for selected currencies in which the rates quoted are against a currency other than the U.S. dollar. The Multicurrency Service automatically converts the transaction currency to the acquirer's settlement currency (if the two are different), and automatically converts the cardholder's billing currency to the issuer's settlement currency (if the two are different), to one of the settlement currencies. text_a: Purchase With Cashback – Cashback is a variation of the purchase transaction permitting the cardholder to get cash in addition to goods or services. Cashback is a domestic service available to participating Visa regions for their issuers, acquirers, and merchants. The VisaNet Cashback Service identifies the cashback amount separately in authorization messages and in settlement to allow issuers to make authorization decisions and to monitor cash activity for their cardholders, Clients can contact their Visa representatives for additional information on cashback features, controls, and availability. Quasi-Cash – Quasi-cash is a variation of the purchase transaction, used for the purchase of items directly convertible to cash, such as gaming chips and money orders. It is available for Visa POS and Interlink. VisaNet does not support American Express Quasi-cash transactions. Key-Entered Purchase – This transaction is a variation of the purchase transaction, used only for Visa POS transactions when the magnetic stripe on the card is not readable. Purchase With Address Verification – This transaction is used by such merchants as direct marketing firms and airlines to verify a cardholder's address as part of a purchase request. This transaction is available for Visa POS.

Account Funding Transaction – This transaction is used to fund accounts such as brokerage accounts and online stored value cards, from a Visa debit or credit card. Original Credit Transaction – This transaction enables funds to be credited to Visa account numbers for a purpose other than refunding a Visa purchase. Deferred Clearing Purchase Transaction – This transaction is used by such merchants as hotels and car rental agencies when the full purchase amount is not known at the time of transaction authorization. This transaction, used only by Visa POS acquirers, involves an authorization request followed by a deferred clearing advice message. Merchandise Return – A merchandise return transaction enables merchants to credit the account of a Visa POS cardholder who returns merchandise. Balance Inquiry – Balance inquiry transactions enable cardholders to check their balances at stand-alone merchant terminals and at the point of sale. If the issuer system cannot be reached, V.I.P. stand-in processing responds that issuer is not available. If the issuer is available and supports balance inquiries, VisaNet returns the account balance to the acquirer for display or for printing in the currency of the merchant or of the ATM. Issuers can optionally provide balance information in Visa POS purchase transaction responses. However, for an 0200 POS eFunds transactions (network 0029), the acquirer receives balance information in Field 54 – Additional Amounts regardless of the issuer's selected response options. (This processing does not apply to stand-alone balance inquiries.) ATM acquirers in the U.S. region must support balance inquiries; support of this transaction is optional for all other participants. PINs are required for full service 0200 POS balance inquiries. PINs may not be required if a chip card is being used in a full service 0100 POS balance inquiries. Address Verification Only (Visa POS) – This transaction is used by merchants like direct marketing firms and airlines to verify a cardholder's address before submitting a purchase transaction. Incremental Authorizations – Merchants use incremental authorization transactions when final purchase amounts are unknown. Incremental authorizations enable merchants to obtain approval on additional amount, after the merchant uses an estimated amount to initiate and authorize the original transaction. Merchants can only do an incremental authorization in conjunction with an estimated authorization. When merchants determine final amounts, they submit supplemental, incremental authorization, or authorization reversal for cancelled purchases. Endpoints must not decline incremental authorizations by treating them as duplicate. In incremental authorization requests and their reversals, field 11 and field 37 values matches corresponding values in original authorization requests and the Transaction identifier (TID) value matches corresponding values in original authorization responses. Acquirers perform clearing using a single clearing transaction for the final amount, the issuer can match the incremental authorizations to the original estimated amount. Participating CPS POS Acquirers must include the TID from the initial authorization in any subsequent incremental authorization request or reversal.
